title: Valuation probe of a scheme specialization with a prescribed generic field
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $u:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ be a morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Write $y\prime$ for the image of its unique point, and let $y\in Y$ be a specialization of $y\prime$, meaning $y\in\overline{\{y\prime\}}$. There exist a valuation subring $A\subseteq K$ with fraction field $K$ [def-trf-valuation-ring] and a morphism $v:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ such that $v$ sends the closed point $\mathfrak m_A$ to $y$ and $v|_{\operatorname{Spec}K}=u$.

source.place: Tag 01J8, lemma-points-specialize, parts (1)-(2), prescribed extension K/kappa(y-prime), with the given field-point morphism; proof using Tag 00IA (algebra-lemma-dominate).

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Y$ containing $y$. Every open containing $y$ contains $y\prime$, since $y\in\overline{\{y\prime\}}$. Thus $u$ restricts to $u_U:\operatorname{Spec}K\to U$ (restrict its continuous map and structure-sheaf map). By the affine-spectrum correspondence write $u_U=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ for $\varphi:R\to K$. Let $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q$ represent $y,y\prime$ in $U$; then $\mathfrak q=\ker\varphi$. Also $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$: otherwise an $a\in\mathfrak q\setminus\mathfrak p$ would make $D(a)$ an open containing $y$ but not $y\prime$.

source.place: Tag 01J8 (lemma-points-specialize), affine form of the first sentence of its proof; Tag 01J7 (lemma-specialize-points), affine-chart argument

proof.text:
Put $S=\varphi(R)\subseteq K$ and $P=\varphi(\mathfrak p)\subseteq S$. This is an ideal, and $\varphi^{-1}(P)=\mathfrak p$, because $\ker\varphi\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Hence $P$ is proper and prime: lift two elements of $S$ to $R$ and apply primality of $\mathfrak p$. Form $B=S_P$. It embeds in $K$ by $s/t\mapsto s/t$, since $S\subseteq K$ and $t
otin P$ implies $t
e0$. The localization node says $B$ is local with maximal ideal $PB$. Its contraction to $S$ is $P$: if $s/1=a/t$ with $a\in P$ and $t
otin P$, then $ts=a$ in the domain $S$, so $s\in P$. Therefore the composite $R	o S	o B$ contracts $\mathfrak m_B$ to $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 01J8 (lemma-points-specialize), local image of the map to K; explicit affine localization of that image

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-local-domain-valuation-dominates] to the local subring $B\subseteq K$. Obtain a valuation subring $A\subseteq K$, with fraction field $K$, containing $B$ and satisfying $\mathfrak m_A\cap B=\mathfrak m_B$. Thus for $\alpha:R\to S\to B\hookrightarrow A$ one has $\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak m_A)=\mathfrak p$.

Define $v$ to be $\operatorname{Spec}A\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Spec}\alpha}U\hookrightarrow Y$. On prime ideals $\operatorname{Spec}\alpha$ acts by inverse image, so the equality just proved sends the closed point to $\mathfrak p$, hence to $y$. The composite $R\xrightarrow{\alpha}A\hookrightarrow K$ is exactly $\varphi$ by the definitions of $S$ and the embedding of $S_P$. Contravariant functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ gives $v\circ\operatorname{Spec}(A\hookrightarrow K)=u_U$ followed by $U\hookrightarrow Y$, which is $u$. This proves the required equality of morphisms, including the prescribed field map.
